xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Assistant Commissioner of Central Tax, Mysuru Rural Division, Mysuru
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs:
GST Refund filed under Section 54 of CGST Act read with Rule 89 of the CGST Rules: Additional Commissioner, Central Tax (Appeals), Mysuru [Appellate authority] allowed department appeals filed by Assistant Commissioner of Central Tax, Mysuru and set aside the favourable GST refund orders passed by Assistant Commissioner of Central Tax, Mysuru. Appellate order confirmed that these as erroneous GST refunds sanctioned under incorrect Rule 89(4) instead of Rule 89 (4B) and holding the refund calculations to be incorrect in some cases.
The Orders-in-Appeals (O-I-A)passed are legally incorrect, bad in law and have been passed without examining the issue properly. Rule 89(4B) has already been omitted on 8-10-2024 and High Courts have held that if any CGST Rule is omitted unconditionally, without a saving clause in favour of the pending proceedings, then all actions from the date of such omission of the rule must stop. Similarly, the calculations adopted in the claim have already been verified and refund sanctioned by the GST authorities appropriately. Hence, O-I-As are incorrect.
The Company has a very strong case. Therefore, the Company expects no financial or operational impact.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Company will file a detailed appeal on merits before the Goods and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT), Bengaluru within the due date (not later than 30.06.2026)
